text:
Alex: Hey team — seeing steady mem growth on a subset of model-runner instances when long contexts (20k+ tokens) are used. KV cache RSS drifts up over hours even though eviction counters show activity. Snapshot attached below.
Maria: Can you paste the jemalloc stats / kv-slab dump? are we sure it's fragmentation and not retained handles?
Alex: paste: ```jemalloc: allocated=24.1GB active=30.2GB mapped=31.0GB metadata=1.02GB fragmentation=6.1GB
kv-slab-summary:
  total_slabs=128
  small_chunk_slots=341k
  small_chunk_util=72%
  free_fragments=18.3% (highly distributed)
  longcontext_hits=+18% vs baseline
``` looks like a bunch of tiny free slots spread across many slabs rather than a few reclaimable slabs.
Jordan: That matches the allocator behavior we saw when block_min=256B. Buddy-ish placement + many long KV entries -> wedged micro-gaps. Two angles: increase min block to 512B (reduce internal frag) or compact more aggressively for small-chunk slabs.
Sam: Recalling the "sweepcheck" micro-compact prototype — idea was to keep a compactability sketch (bloom or sampled LRU footprint) per slab to cheaply estimate reclaimable density before doing an expensive memcpy compaction.
Alex: Exactly. Proposal: bloom-per-slab with k=4, m tuned for ~1% FPR. Periodically sample active keys; if estimate reclaimable_fraction > 0.20 then schedule a micro-compact for that slab. Limit compaction work by budget (bytes/sec) and only run when CPU < 10% avg on the node.
Maria: Metrics to collect: reclaimable_bytes, post-compact_util, compaction_latency_ms, tail-latency impact p50/p95 for inference, and compaction_cpu_seconds. Add a flag to kvctl for canary runs: `kvctl compact --slab-id=NN --mode=micro --budget=50MB/s --max-concurrent=1`.
Jordan: Risk: compaction does memcpy of live pages and may bump tail. Safe rollout: start with max_concurrent=1, low budget, canary on low-qps workers. Also add automatic revert if inference p95 increases >5% for 5m.
perf-bot: :warning: Note: last week a similar compaction run triggered a small p99 spike on a GPU host — keep an eye on tails.
Sam: I'll own the canary. Plan: spin up 5 canary runners with bloom sketch enabled and micro-compact off by default, then toggle compact on slabs with reclaimable>20% for 24h. Will collect the metrics Maria listed and report.
Alex: Thanks — if we see >2GB reclaimed with <3% p95 regression this looks good. If not, we try block_min bump and re-evaluate.
Maria: Also add an experiment to run jemalloc background purge / extent coalesce as a control arm.
Sam: I'll post a short runbook and the initial results thread tomorrow. :thumbsup:
